courses.title: Introduction to the Profession
courses.course_description: Introduces the student to the scope of mathematics as a profession, develops a sense of mathematical curiosity and problem solving skills, identifies and reinforces the student's career choices, and provides a mechanism for regular academic advising. Emphasis is placed on the development of teamwork skills.

courses.title: Linear Mathematics
courses.course_description: This course introduces the mathematics of linear systems that underlie many modern applications in business, data analysis, economics, and information technology. Students study linear equations and inequalities, matrix methods for solving systems, linear transformations, and linear optimization, with an emphasis on modeling and interpreting real-world problems such as resource allocation and economic input–output models. The course also includes an introduction to Markov chains, which use matrices to model systems that evolve over time, such as decision processes and long-term trends. Throughout the course, students build quantitative reasoning skills and learn to use algebraic, graphical, and matrix-based tools to analyze practical problems, focusing on insight, interpretation, and application.

courses.title: Linear Algebra: Theory/Appl
courses.course_description: This course develops the fundamental concepts of linear algebra and their role in modeling and solving problems arising in science, engineering, and data analysis. Topics include systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, vector spaces, linear transformations, orthogonality, and inner product spaces. Students learn how these ideas reveal the structure of high-dimensional systems and support important computational techniques such as least squares and matrix factorizations. Emphasis is placed on both mathematical understanding and practical applications of linear algebra.

courses.title: Probability/Statistics for ECE
courses.course_description: This course focuses on the introductory treatment of probability theory including: axioms of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, random vectors, marginal, joint, conditional and cumulative probability distributions, moment generating functions, expectations, and correlations. Also covered are sums of random variables, central limit theorem, sample means, and parameter estimation. Furthermore, random processes and random signals are covered. Examples and applications are drawn from problems of importance to electrical and computer engineers. Credit only granted for one of MATH 374, MATH 474, and MATH 475.

courses.title: Com Linear Algebra Sci and Eng
courses.course_description: This course explores how linear algebra is used in practice to solve large, real-world problems in data science, engineering, and science. Students learn how matrix algorithms are implemented on computers and why issues such as accuracy, stability, and efficiency matter when working with real data. Through hands-on programming and applied examples, students gain experience with core computational tools including matrix factorizations, least-squares methods, and iterative solvers for linear and nonlinear equations. By the end of the course, students will be equipped with practical skills in numerical linear algebra that are directly applicable to technical careers, research, and graduate study.

courses.course_description: The course provides a systematic approach to modeling applications from areas such as physics and chemistry, engineering, biology, and business (operations research).
